findings.text: The committed arc bar's right edge encodes ratio 1.2308 from the retired 3328 while the receipt it cites now gives 1.6623 from 154; re-rendering changes exactly the two arc bars, so the figure rests on the retired capture.

The arc_capacity table row still shows observed 3072, 3328 with ratios 1.33, 1.23, superseded by the regenerated receipt's 152, 154 and 1.6842, 1.6623; the bucket-floor followup argues the coarse floor from this table.
The section still discloses the in-process _UNIT_NODE shim and the framework_compat_shims receipt key, both retired by the reviewed commit and now refused by the guard.
The claim that the census figures are unaffected so no figure was regenerated enumerates counts only; the left panel's arc bars are drawn from a ratio that moved between the two captures.
The bar-value test holds only the two caption counts in the SVG to the receipt, not the per-axis ratio bars the renderer draws, so a figure drawn from the retired capture passes the gate.

justifications.durability: The receipt is regenerated by the driver rather than edited, the guard is a committed test that refuses the pre-change receipt, and the commits carry bodies naming what moved.
justifications.evidence: The control reproduces leaf for leaf from the node's own artifact and the gate log backs the guard, but the "figures unaffected" consequence is asserted from counts without checking the renderer's data path.
justifications.fit: The plan's design doc and the bucket figure still quote the retired 3072/3328 and the retired shim disclosure that the plan's next item argues from.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The two things the goal names hold — the shim is dead (grep + the reproduced AttributeError) and all three groups of moved leaves are attributed correctly, with the one-node-caused group distinguished from the refactor and the live cache capture.
justifications.scope_discipline: Writes stay inside the declared paths, the scope grep residue is reported as out-of-scope dead code with its AttributeError rather than as clean, and the cache-pin drift is recorded as a deviation instead of hidden.

raw_text: # Review — merged census shim deletion (18287b1b, 7760e645, merged c16dd729) Node: review-of-msc-delete-observation-shim (role review, plan nova:millisecond-converged-solve) Reviewed run: r-20260919T140415194531-msc-delete-observation-shim (msc-delete-observation-shim, base 1f9fe3cf) Reviewed head: c16dd729 (merge msc-delete-observation-shim) — present in this worktree's history Review head: 10f8c68df VERDICT: pass — the shim is truly dead, the control is sound and reproduces first-hand, the arc_capacity attribution to the traced-polygon capacity refactor holds with the producing commits named below, and the receipt guard fires on the pre-change receipt. One claim in the landing record is under-inclusive and two artifacts outside the node's write paths still rest on the retired capture; both are recorded below and carried to the plan's bucket-floor followup. ## 1. Is the census shim dead, and does anything else still publish onto nova.equilibrium.observation? Dead. Named by grep over benchmarks/, nova/, tests/: - `benchmarks/program_shape_census.py` no longer names `observation` at all: the only `observation` hits in the whole tree under benchmarks/, nova/ and tests/ are `benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py:3702` (`len(clip_quadrature._UNIT_NODE)`), `nova/equilibrium/clip_quadrature.py:30` (the definition), the five write sites and one read under `certificate.observation._UNIT_NODE` below, and `tests/test_solovev_certificate_builder.py:16,53,54,59` (a deliberate negative control). `grep -rn "_UNIT_NODE" benchmarks/program_shape_census.py` returns nothing. - The five remaining production write sites are on `certificate.observation`, i.e. the `benchmarks.solovev_certificate` namespace, not `nova.equilibrium.observation`: `benchmarks/exact_clip_memory_scenario...` — precisely `benchmarks/exact_clip_memory_scaling.py:202,278,573`, `benchmarks/exact_clip_warm_cost.py:333` and `tests/test_exact_clip_memory.py:68` (write) plus `:175` (read). They are dead, verified by running the guarded expression, not by reading it: certificate is .../benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py hasattr(certificate, 'observation'): False raising it: AttributeError module 'benchmarks.solovev_certificate' has no attribute 'observation' hasattr(nova.equilibrium.observation, '_UNIT_NODE'): False Every site is guarded by `if not hasattr(certificate.observation, "_UNIT_NODE")`, so the guard is false and no publication happens. The node's record states this residue as out-of-scope dead code with the AttributeError quoted (`docs/evidence/archive/millisecond-converged-solve-landed.html:824`) rather than reporting a clean scope grep — accurate, and the claim reproduces exactly. - One writer onto `nova.equilibrium.observation` itself remains and is intentional: `tests/test_solovev_certificate_builder.py:59` monkeypatches a foreign object onto it (`from nova.equilibrium import observation`, line 16) to assert it cannot supply the dimension, and pytest reverts it. That is a negative control, not a live shim. ## 2. Is the node's control sound, and does it show the shim was not load-bearing? Reproduced first-hand on the login node with `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python`, the pre-change driver at `18287b1b^` (shim intact, extracted to `control/program_shape_census_prechange.py`) against the current builder: observation._UNIT_NODE present before the call: False driver publishes the shim when absent: True weak-rotation-reactor-static arc_capacity= 152 support_capacity= 24 moderate-rotation-conventional-static arc_capacity= 152 support_capacity= 24 strong-rotation-compact-static arc_capacity= 152 support_capacity= 24 diverted-single-null arc_capacity= 154 support_capacity= 26 arc_capacity vector: [152, 152, 152, 154] observation._UNIT_NODE present after the call: False That matches the node's own control artifact (`reports/nova/s19-local/msc-delete-observation-shim/control-with-shim.json`, captured 2026-09-19T16:18:34+0200, `framework_compat_shims` present) leaf for leaf: the same 152,152,152,154 with support 24,24,24,26. The shim fired (the attribute was absent, so the driver published it) and the arc capacity did not move, so driver-side shim removal cannot be the cause. The code path agrees: the shim supplies only `quadrature_nodes_per_axis`, while `arc_capacity` is read from `separatrix_clip.traced_polygon_vertex_capacity(chord_capacity)` at `benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py:3702`. The control is sound and it establishes the claim it was run for. ## 3. Does the attribution of the arc_capacity move to the traced-polygon refactor hold? Holds, and is sharper than the record states. `nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py:78` returns `_SPLINE_BOUNDARY_SEGMENTS + int(straight_vertex_capacity)` with `_SPLINE_BOUNDARY_SEGMENTS = 128` at line 54: 128 + 24 = 152 and 128 + 26 = 154, exactly the regenerated receipt's vector. The retired capture's 3072/3328 is the swept product the builder used to compute itself: `git show f6bce45ed^:benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py` line 3654 reads `exact_capacity = chord_capacity * chain_samples`, i.e. 24 × 128 = 3072 and 26 × 128 = 3328. Two commits together produce the move, and the record names only the mechanism: - `f7fefbd78` (2026-09-17, refactor(equilibrium): size the traced polygon capacity to its realised layout) replaces the per-slot product with the sum in the library and adds `traced_polygon_vertex_capacity`; - `f6bce45ed` (2026-09-18 10:26, fix(benchmarks): derive the memory receipts support capacity from the bound) switches the builder's `exact_support_capacity` to that function. The retired capture (2026-09-18T00:52:36+0200) predates f6bce45ed and reads the product; the regenerated capture (2026-09-19T16:13:23+0200) postdates both and reads the sum. The record's "the move is the traced-polygon capacity refactor" is correct at the level of mechanism; these two SHAs are the precise attribution. ## 4. Does the receipt guard now refuse a census carrying a compatibility shim? Yes, with both arms run first-hand (`/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider`): - Positive control, current receipt: `7 passed in 3.43s`, exit 0 (`control/gate-current-receipt.log`). - Negative arm, the pre-change receipt (`18287b1b^` content swapped in at the receipt path for one run, then restored): `2 failed, 5 passed in 5.00s`, exit 1 (`control/gate-prechange-receipt.log`), and one failure is the flipped guard itself: tests/test_census_record_receipts.py:131: AssertionError: E AssertionError: the census must carry no compatibility shim E assert 'framework_compat_shims' not in {...'captured_at': '2026-09-18T00:52:36+0200'...} The other failure is the cache-capture pin, expected with the older capture. The receipt was restored byte-identical (sha256 `d1895127ccce0083bee1ffed9963dd9dff84b0c11f5c147759e62b6c9cf0f81a`, matching the pre-swap digest) and `git status --short` is clean. ## 5. Does any figure or downstream number still rest on the retired 3072 arc capacity? Yes — two artifacts, neither regenerated, both outside this node's write paths (`follow_ons`): - **The bucket figure's arc bars.** `render_buckets.py:34-39` draws one bar per observed capacity from `receipt["combined"]["padding_waste"][axis]["padding_ratio"]`, arc_capacity included. Re-rendering from the current receipt (`control/rerender/`) changes exactly 2 of 80 path elements — the two arc bars: committed right edges `155.980979`/`152.443028` (ratios 1.3333/1.2308 from 3072/3328) against fresh `168.092853`/`167.336939` (1.6842/1.6623 from 152/154). So the committed `program-shape-buckets.svg` (and its PNG twin) still encode the retired capture, while the receipt it cites as its source says otherwise. - **`docs/research/compile-cost-evidence.html` §4**, the design doc the plan links: line 85 still discloses the in-process compatibility shim and the `framework_compat_shims` receipt key, both retired by the reviewed commit; line 93 still says "arc capacities of 3,072, 3,072, 3,072 and 3,328"; line 95 still carries the table row `arc_capacity256, 512, 1024, 20483072, 33281.33, 1.23` against the receipt's 152, 154 and 1.6842, 1.6623; and the §4 cache sentence still reads 3,958 entries / 18.662 GiB / 2.2 days against the fresh capture's 3,989 / 18.713 GiB / 3.9 days. The bucket-floor followup is `f-msc-bucket-floor-measure` (the plan's own `next` item, which argues the coarse mesh-cell floor from these very padding ratios), so it would consume the stale arc row and the stale figure. Consequence for the node's record: its sentence at `docs/evidence/archive/millisecond-converged-solve-landed.html:821` — "The census figures are unaffected: bank identities 12, combined identities 16, 5 capacity vectors today and 2 bucketed programs all stand, so no figure was regenerated" — is true of the enumerated counts and the right panel, and false of the left panel, whose arc bars are drawn from a ratio that moved; the Artifacts paragraph repeats it as "the census figure it guards is unchanged". The older 2026-09-18 archive paragraph (`:736`, "arc 3072 to 3328") is a dated landing record and the node's own new section states the move, so it is a timeline artifact rather than a live claim. Contributing cause: `tests/test_census_record_receipts.py:97` is named for the bucket bar values but holds only the two caption counts (lines 108-112) to the receipt, not the per-axis bars the renderer draws — which is why a figure drawn from the retired capture passes the gate. ## The five dimension scores SCORE goal_fidelity: 16 JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: The two things the goal names hold — the shim is dead (grep + the reproduced AttributeError) and all three groups of moved leaves are attributed correctly, with the one-node-caused group distinguished from the refactor and the live cache capture.
